name: beyond
label: BEYOND-HUMAN, not a human profile. A LABELLED BODY VARIANT with invented multipliers. Its results are never to be compared with the average, P95, elite2 or sprinter trials, and say nothing about human sprinting.

about: A hypothetical body that is not human: the elite-sprinter body (profiles/sprinter.json) scaled UP by round numbers. It exists to answer one question for the control plane: can the same runner family (RunGearXSkill: the gears, the mean-of-seeds search, the standing start) be tuned to a fall-free standing-start peak speed above 10 m/s on a body whose muscles are strong and fast enough for that, and what did that body need. It is NOT a claim about human sprinting: 10 m/s and beyond is beyond every measured person on this model (calibrated so that the average man's ideal-control ceiling is 8.2 m/s, P95's 10.45, the sprinter's 12.36). Every note, page text and README line about it says BEYOND-HUMAN.
population: none: an invented body, stronger and faster than any person in every muscle group

rule.text: The body is the sprinter profile scaled UP by round numbers (strength multiplier and speed multiplier from the ladder; tendon x1.5 and activation x0.8 exactly as the sprinter; anthropometry unchanged, the average 1.75 m / 67.5 kg skeleton), and it is the SMALLEST ladder step whose ideal-control ceiling is above 14.5 m/s, so that 10 m/s is about 70 % of the ceiling (the runner family reached 68 % of the sprinter's ceiling, 79 % of P95's, 75 % of the average body's, 73 % of elite2's).
rule.ceiling: the stance-budget ceiling at t_sw 0.35 s, the same estimator and recipe as the other bodies: playground/sprint_limits.py speeds --pitch-free, driven by scratchpad/sprint_knot/ceiling_probe.py (v4 anatomy, ROBOLAB_BODY=v4 ROBOLAB_CALIB=v4, the four muscle parts, two restarts per speed, --cycle 0, --stop budget, 1 m/s spacing warm-started from the sprinter's solutions) and scratchpad/sprint_knot/budget_ceiling.py at t_sw 0.35 (the point estimate, no tolerance).
rule.at_most_two_ceilings: At most two candidates get a measured ceiling: steps 1 and 2 (run at the same time to save wall clock). The pick: step 1 if its ceiling is above 14.5 m/s; else step 2 if its ceiling is above 14.5; else step 3 WITHOUT a further stretch and without waiting for its ceiling (which is then measured afterwards, if time allows, and reported as it is).
rule.unchanged_from_sprinter: tendon x1.5, activation x0.8 (10 -> 8 ms, 40 -> 32 ms), anthropometry 1.0 / 1.0
rule.stretch: THE MULTIPLIERS ARE AN INVENTED STRETCH. No measurement, distribution or literature value stands behind strength x2.0-3.0 or speed x1.7-2.4 on top of a model whose peak forces are already 1.4-2.9x young men's voluntary maxima; they are round numbers chosen so that a stronger body exists, not estimates of anything living.

step1.chain: v4b_beyondc1_s1 (10-15 m/s; its margin-line fit says 14.53, the rule names the budget estimator)

decision.pick: step 2: the smallest ladder step whose ceiling (budget_ceiling.py at t_sw 0.35) is above 14.5 m/s. Step 3 was not needed and not computed.
decision.estimator: the sprinter's: sprint_limits.py speeds --pitch-free, ceiling_probe.py --cycle 0 --stop budget, 1 m/s spacing from the sprinter's 10 m/s solution, two restarts per speed; one sparse chain per candidate (+-0.5-0.7 m/s as for the other bodies). Data out/sprint_limits/probe_v4b_beyondc{1,2}_s1_v*; for the other bodies: average 8.20, P95 10.45, elite2 9.28, sprinter 12.36.
decision.reading: 10 m/s is 61 % of this body's ideal-control ceiling of 16.32 m/s (the rule wanted about 70 %; the ladder has no step between 13.51 and 16.32).

strength.stat: peak isometric force per kg body mass, the same multiplier on every muscle group: ladder step 2; x2.4 = the sprinter's x1.55 stretched by x1.55
strength.note: INVENTED. Not literature, not a percentile. The sprinter's x1.55 was already a stretch above the measured range for the knee and ankle extensors.

speed.stat: maximum joint angular velocity = fibre shortening velocity x fascicle length: ladder step 2; x2.0 = the sprinter's x1.45 stretched by x1.38, one multiplier for every joint
speed.note: INVENTED. Above the sprinter range derived from fibre mix and fascicle length (x1.3-1.5).

tendon.stat: tendon stiffness per unit body size x1.5: UNCHANGED from the P95 and sprinter profiles
tendon.note: Kept at the sprinter's value on purpose, so the beyond body differs from the sprinter in muscle force and muscle speed only.

activation.stat: activation and deactivation time constants x0.8: UNCHANGED from the sprinter profile
activation.note: Kept at the sprinter's unverified x0.8.

anthro.stat: the average body's 1.75 m / 67.5 kg (segment lengths and masses after Winter's tables): UNCHANGED
anthro.note: 1.0 / 1.0, so ROBOLAB_PROFILE_PARTS=all builds the same XML as ROBOLAB_PROFILE_PARTS=strength,speed,tendon,activation.

relation_to_other_bodies.sprinter: strength x2.4 / 1.55 = x1.55 and speed x2.0 / 1.45 = x1.38; tendon, activation and anthropometry the same
relation_to_other_bodies.p95: strength x2.4 / 1.32 = x1.82 and speed x2.0 / 1.2 = x1.67
relation_to_other_bodies.reading: a result on this body says what the control plane can do when the body is strong and fast enough, and which of the runner's pieces had to be re-searched for it; it is not comparable with any human trial
